nodes.label: Flight parabolas and flight cost
nodes.rationale: A flight of L units costs 25 + 1.5 L + L^2/100 against 1 per unit driven, so the search flies only where the road does not go. Chosen while looking at the 17 tracks, so results are not a held-out test.

nodes.label: Route built from track geometry alone
nodes.norm_label: route built from track geometry alone
nodes.rationale: The 352-input observation includes the human lap's line, speeds and keys, so the agent cannot run on a track with no human lap; a route from start, ordered checkpoints and finish removes that dependency. It is the shortest way, not the fastest, with no cornering-speed model.

nodes.label: 334-number reference-free observation
nodes.rationale: Replaces human-line entries with route points, curvature, route frame, slope, on-road flags, flight and gate entries. Human speed and keys are gone and not replaced: nothing derived from the track says how fast a corner can be taken.

nodes.label: Route progress measure (tracker)
nodes.rationale: Progress along the route is meant to be the ruler for a lap-free environment; tested by 'off pace' rather than distance, since wide human lines are far from the route yet keep step.

nodes.label: Staged shortest-path search with heading
nodes.rationale: One stage per gate; heading carried in the state (max 67 degree step) so the path cannot reverse on a 13-unit road, and rim-running is forbidden to keep it off beams and kerb crests.

nodes.label: summer4 and desert5 routes diverge from the human
nodes.norm_label: summer4 and desert5 routes diverge from the human
nodes.rationale: On summer4 the wall-top hop costs less than two designed flights (700), and the wall-top surface is real so no geometric rule excludes it.

nodes.label: Surface graph of the collision mesh
nodes.norm_label: surface graph of the collision mesh
nodes.rationale: Joining sampled points by normal (within 37 degrees) keeps road and wall apart while keeping a loop or banked wall in one piece.

nodes.label: Defect: progress keeps counting for a car under a raised road
nodes.norm_label: defect: progress keeps counting for a car under a raised road
nodes.rationale: Not fixed: whether progress should freeze or the episode should end with no road under the car is the author's design decision, and the same choice decides what happens in flight.

nodes.label: Chain generator with depth-first backtracking
nodes.rationale: Lets a generalist train on hundreds of tracks instead of 17; hills emerge from matching pitches rather than a rule about hills. Only narrow-road chains: about a third of what official tracks are built from.

nodes.label: Drivable ground at height 0 and the raised road default
nodes.norm_label: drivable ground at height 0 and the raised road default
nodes.rationale: A car leaving a level-0 road carries on across the ground, so leaving the road could not be told from staying on it; raising the road to level 2 makes finishing mean having stayed on the road.

nodes.label: Piece table and ports derived from collision triangles
nodes.norm_label: piece table and ports derived from collision triangles
nodes.rationale: Ports are boundary edges of the upward-facing surface on a grid plane with no kerb or wall, so pieces can be chained without storing any of the game's geometry.

nodes.label: Scripted follower as proof of drivability
nodes.norm_label: scripted follower as proof of drivability
nodes.rationale: A proof that a generated track can be finished, not a fast lap; its lap is a poor reference for speed (about 110 km/h down the middle).

nodes.label: Speed ladder: telling an impossible track from a weak driver
nodes.norm_label: speed ladder: telling an impossible track from a weak driver
nodes.rationale: A failed drive proves nothing alone; structure checks do not use the driver, and failing fast but finishing slow indicates a weak driver. The argument ends once jumps are added.

nodes.label: watchLap: is the track's own surface under the car
nodes.norm_label: watchlap: is the track's own surface under the car
nodes.rationale: The mesh from loadTrackInfo holds only the track's parts, never the ground plane, so a ray straight down tells road from grass; offered as the general answer for other ideas.

nodes.label: Cell archive (20 units by 2 units sideways)
nodes.norm_label: cell archive (20 units by 2 units sideways)
nodes.rationale: A cell keeps the state that reached it soonest; picked with weight 1/(1+tries). Off-line cells moved the frontier less often but this is confounded with closeness to a crash, so not acted on.

nodes.label: Continuation kinds: sample, hot, kick, lift
nodes.norm_label: continuation kinds: sample, hot, kick, lift
nodes.rationale: No kind is clearly better (10 to 16% of restarts move the frontier), so all four stay.

nodes.label: Go-Explore style exploration from save states
nodes.norm_label: go-explore style exploration from save states
nodes.rationale: On an unseen track, restarting a little before where the furthest attempt ended and keeping what gets further finds one finished lap, which can become imitation examples for a short fine-tune.

nodes.label: Restart back-off levels 1.5 / 3 / 5 s
nodes.rationale: 0 of 33 restarts from more than 5 s behind the frontier moved it, against 33 of 195 from closer; 1.5 to 3 s is the best single distance.

nodes.label: Backing up up to 3 s after a dead end
nodes.norm_label: backing up up to 3 s after a dead end
nodes.rationale: Without it desert3 seeds 11 and 12 ended off track at 53.4% with all 25 continuations failing; horizon 40 with backing up beat horizon 80 without. Not free on other laps.

nodes.label: Failure rule: cut off by environment or too slow at the horizon
nodes.norm_label: failure rule: cut off by environment or too slow at the horizon
nodes.rationale: The too-slow rule (below 0.4x the human's speed) is needed because 'stalled' only fires 2 s after the car stops, which is the whole horizon.

nodes.label: Lazy mode: alternatives only when the policy's continuation fails
nodes.norm_label: lazy mode: alternatives only when the policy's continuation fails
nodes.rationale: Chosen as default: full mode took 73x ticks and a slower lap (22.773 s vs 19.819 s) on winter4 seed 10, and lazy leaves a good driver exactly alone.

nodes.label: Lookahead driver (driveLap)
nodes.rationale: The simulator is exact, so a try-out that crashes would have crashed for real; saving state and trying continuations 2 s ahead makes a policy robust on unseen tracks. A robustness tool, not a speed tool.

nodes.label: Scoring continuations: reward, progress or value
nodes.norm_label: scoring continuations: reward, progress or value
nodes.rationale: Reward stays the default because it is the only one that charges for hitting things inside the horizon; two seeds do not separate the scores.

nodes.label: Caveat: comparison is not at equal simulated cost
nodes.norm_label: caveat: comparison is not at equal simulated cost
nodes.rationale: One plain attempt is compared to a lookahead lap costing 9 to 39 plain laps; at equal cost (g2-3 logs) winter4 is the only track where lookahead does what retries do not.

nodes.label: Design A: recurrent RL-squared policy (not built)
nodes.norm_label: design a: recurrent rl-squared policy (not built)
nodes.rationale: Would need to learn across 2000 to 3500 decisions with 256-step rollouts, a sequence trainer and a recurrent Node actor; not to be started before B is shown to fall short.

nodes.label: Design B: attempt-conditioned inputs (built)
nodes.rationale: No PPO changes, warm-starts from the generalist with zero memory weights, and the map can be printed and read when it does not work. Limit: cannot remember what nobody put in the map.

nodes.label: MemoryEnv sessions of consecutive attempts
nodes.rationale: Session length 1 to sessionMax drawn afresh so first tries keep being practised and every update holds every attempt number.

nodes.label: session_advantages with carry across attempts
nodes.rationale: Passes A's cross-attempt credit through the critic: add carry x the value of the next attempt's first observation, giving B the objective of exploring on purpose with 3 changed lines.

nodes.label: Track memory map indexed by progress (2-unit bins)
nodes.norm_label: track memory map indexed by progress (2-unit bins)
nodes.rationale: Crash sites repeat (desert3: 15 of 15 crashes at three places), which is the case a position-indexed crash map is for. Speed and lateral offset are recorded because they are what the policy can most directly act on.
